culturalBackground: Finger-only mehndi is a popular minimal choice for people who want a small design that is quick to apply.
Filling the fingertips solid with henna is a traditional look in many regions, from South Asia to North Africa.
Ring-style bands drawn around one or more fingers imitate jewelry and pair well with a bare palm.
Fingertips have thick skin, so they usually take the darkest stain on the hand.
applicationTips: Keep the fingers slightly apart while the paste dries so neighbouring designs do not touch.
Use a fine-tipped cone; finger designs leave little room for thick lines.
Avoid bending the fingers until the paste is dry, or the lines across the knuckles will crack.

faqPool.q: How long does a finger mehndi design take?
faqPool.a: A simple finger design takes about 10 to 15 minutes per hand, which makes it a good last-minute option.

faqPool.q: Why are fingertips often filled in completely?
faqPool.a: Solid fingertips are a traditional style in several henna cultures, and the thick skin there gives a deep, lasting stain.

faqPool.q: Can I do finger mehndi on myself?
faqPool.a: Yes. It is one of the easiest placements to do yourself, though the hand you write with is harder to decorate.
